Definition: to complete, in a good or a bad sense, literal, or figurative, transitive or intransitive
BiblicalUsage: The priests stand firm on dry ground in the midst of Jordan, until all the people have passed clean over. And Moses makes an end of writing the words of the law in a book, until they are finished. The word is to complete, to finish, to end: a crossing completed, and a book completed, both when the work is done.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe completion is the Bible's quiet promise: the priests stand until all have passed over, and Moses writes until the book is finished, and God does not leave His work half done.
